resolvedExceptions: Authorized users can modify penalty records only before invoice finalization
resolvedConflictsOrObsolete: Earlier lifecycle guidance may have included a tolerance window for early cancellation that would waive penalties, but this exemption language appears to be missing from current documentation
resolutionNotes: R97b defines the penalty application rule with multiple operational requirements covering late returns, damage incidents, penalty management, and dispute workflows. PRIMARY evidence (E1–E12) establishes core behaviors: penalties are calculated based on configured rules, associated with rent records, included in invoices, and subject to authorized modification before finalization. A critical gap exists regarding a potential early-cancellation tolerance window that may have been removed from documentation without explicit decision (E1, E5). The exact penalty calculation formula and configurable rule parameters remain undefined (E6, E9). Dispute resolution and audit logging requirements are specified but depend on clarification of user-identity handling in logs (E3, E6). CONTEXT evidence (E13) refines the lateness threshold definition. Implementation I94b (E7) addresses late return penalty calculation. The requirement is well-scoped operationally but contains material gaps in rule finalization and historical exception handling. Filtered abstract or low-relevance operative statements: System applies penalties for late returns based on configured penalty rules | System applies penalties for damage incidents | Penalties are associated with rent records and included in invoices
